solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Using images, sadly proclaim hate (12)

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are in a sorry disorder

annotation.surface: Someone lamenting that a speech full of imagery was used to proclaim hatred.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma after 'images' makes 'Using images' look like a stage direction, but it is the definition; everything after it is the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: metaphorical language works by images, describing one thing as another.

entries.clue: Captivate attention of number coming up, welcoming tea (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means rising from bottom to top, so the number reads backwards
to welcome someone is to take them in, so the reversed number holds the tea

blocks.note: cha is a slang word for tea

annotation.surface: A performer captivating the attention of the next act to come on, over a cup of tea.
annotation.walkthrough: ENIN opens up and CHA goes into the middle. 'Number' is a plain number here, not a song or an anaesthetic.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: to enchain is literally to put in chains, so to hold someone's attention captive.

entries.clue: After first-class exploit, move carefully forward if necessary (2,1,5)

indicators.note: 'after' puts the first-class letter first and the exploit and the move after it

blocks.note: A = first-class, as in A1 or grade A
to tap a resource is to exploit it
to move slowly and carefully, a little at a time

annotation.surface: Advice to a climber or soldier: after a fine exploit, creep forward only if you must.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' reads as a noun (a daring deed) but works as the verb TAP.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: at a pinch means in an emergency, when really pushed.

entries.clue: The man gathering papers, obscure (4)

indicators.note: to gather something is to take it in and hold it, so the man's letters enclose the papers

annotation.surface: A man collecting some papers that turn out to be obscure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective describing the papers, but it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as a verb, to obscure a thing is to conceal it from view.

entries.clue: Daughter introduced to complicated dress rule with no clear aim (10)

indicators.note: to be introduced to a group is to join it, so D goes in with the letters
complicated means tangled, so the letters of 'dress rule' are jumbled

annotation.surface: A daughter confronted with a baffling dress code that seems to have no point.
annotation.walkthrough: D joins the letters of DRESS RULE before they are rearranged.
annotation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a boat without a rudder cannot be steered, so it drifts without direction.

entries.clue: Urgently need word of warning about Romeo? (5)

indicators.note: about in its sense of 'around': the warning word is wrapped round Romeo

blocks.note: cave (Latin 'beware') was the old British schoolboy lookout's cry
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Juliet's nurse wanting to shout a warning about Romeo.
annotation.walkthrough: CAVE, said 'kay-vee', is the Latin for 'beware' shouted by a pupil keeping watch for a teacher; R sits after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to long for something so strongly that it feels like a need.

entries.clue: One spotted senior church figure, American friend in brief (7)

blocks.note: Leo is a name taken by many popes
pard is US slang, short for pardner (partner)

annotation.surface: Someone who caught sight of a bishop and a Yankee pal together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One spotted' reads as 'one person who was seen', but it means an animal with spots.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the big cat is the classic spotted animal, and 'spotted' pretends to mean 'seen'.

entries.clue: Regularly unsound, complain with exchange of letters, engineer a refusal to budge (13)

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so letters are taken at every second position
an exchange is a swap, so two letters inside the word trade places

blocks.note: the A and I of COMPLAIN change places

annotation.surface: A grumble about a moody engineer who will not shift.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'exchange of letters' is small: only A and I trade places.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: declining to go along with a demand is refusing to budge.

entries.clue: One over the eight, referring to sweetener? (5,3,5)

definitions.note: the first definition describes a drunk person; the answer is a phrase meaning drunk

blocks.note: 'one over the eight' is British slang for someone drunk, having had one pint too many
a sweetener is a bribe, a payment made in secret

annotation.surface: A drinker asking whether the eighth pint counts as a sweetener.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sweetener' suggests sugar, but it is a bribe, paid under the table. Drinking someone under the table means outlasting them, so it also means very drunk.
annotation.definitionFit: Two idioms: drunk enough to slide off one's chair, and paid covertly, out of sight beneath the table.

entries.clue: Fruit here as alternative to vegetable (7)

annotation.surface: A greengrocer offering fruit in place of vegetables.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fruit here' is a definition by place: where fruit grows.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by place: 'Fruit here' names the ground where fruit trees grow.

entries.clue: After return, no opening for difficult criminal force (7)

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters are read in reverse
an opening is a first letter, and 'no opening' takes it away from 'difficult'

annotation.surface: A tough criminal gets no chance to break back in after returning.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Force' is a verb here, not a police force.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to dragoon, from the mounted soldiers once used to enforce order, is to coerce.

entries.clue: Mammal’s outside layer is trimmed (5)

indicators.note: trimming cuts the end off, so the last letter of 'is' goes

blocks.note: an outer layer, as of paint or fur
IS with its last letter trimmed

annotation.surface: An animal's outer fur has been clipped.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'the mammal's coat is trimmed', but the apostrophe-s only joins the definition to the wordplay, and 'is' is itself the word being cut.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the coati is one mammal, a raccoon relative from the Americas.

entries.clue: To beloved, this possibly endears one ultimately? (8)

definitions.text: To beloved, this possibly endears one ultimately?

indicators.note: 'possibly' says the letters could be something else, so they are rearranged
ultimately means at the end, so take the final letter of 'one'

annotation.surface: A lover hoping a song will finally win over the one they adore.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: what is offered to a beloved in hope that it endears the giver at last.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: a song sung beneath a loved one's window is meant, in the end, to win their heart.

entries.clue: Discredit dreadful vigilante ad, no good (10)

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the letters are a mess to be rearranged
'no good' means without G, so the letter is taken out

blocks.note: g = good; removed, leaving VIILANTEAD to be rearranged

annotation.surface: Rubbishing a badly made advert for a vigilante group.
annotation.walkthrough: Remove the G first, then rearrange the ten letters left.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to show a claim is unsound is to discredit it.

entries.clue: Trouble in my glance? (10)

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up and disturb it, so the letters are disturbed

annotation.surface: Someone warning that their look means trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trouble' reads as a noun, but it is the instruction to rearrange; the whole clue also describes a threatening look.
annotation.definitionFit: An &lit: a look that promises trouble is a threatening one, which is how the answer describes it.

entries.clue: Revise course after reflection (4)

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: a tide is a course or flow, as in the tide of events

annotation.surface: Advice to rethink one's plan once one has had time to reflect.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Course' suggests a plan of action or a class, but here it is the flow of water.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to correct and rework a text is to revise it.

entries.clue: Loyal contestant missing outside of Tralee? (8)

indicators.note: a contestant missing something lacks it, so letters are taken away
the outside of a word is its two ends, first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of TraleE, removed from the middle of CONTESTANT

annotation.surface: A faithful competitor fails to show up outside Tralee.
annotation.walkthrough: Tralee is an Irish town that hosts the Rose of Tralee festival, a contest, which gives the surface its logic.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a constant friend is faithful and unchanging, the old sense of steadfast.

entries.clue: Lean piece of veal is tempting (4)

indicators.note: a piece of something is a fragment of it, so the answer is a stretch of the following letters

annotation.surface: A butcher remarking that a lean cut of veal looks tempting.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lean' looks like an adjective describing the veal, but it is the verb, as a ship leans.
annotation.definitionFit: A nautical sense: a ship that tilts to one side is said to do this.

entries.clue: On visit for while, give information about river (7)

indicators.note: about in its sense of 'around': SING wraps round the river

blocks.note: an informer sings to the police
the Tay is a Scottish river

annotation.surface: A visitor passing on some news about the local river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Give information' is slang: an informer who talks to the police is said to sing.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: guests who are with you on a visit for a while are lodging with you.

entries.clue: Difficult situation — island, extremely tense, emotional (10)

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so keep only the first and last letters

blocks.note: as in 'things have come to a pretty pass'
first and last letters of TensE

annotation.surface: A fraught scene on an island, tense and full of feeling.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Island' is usually I in crosswords; here it is a whole island.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: feelings running high make a person strongly emotional.

entries.clue: Firm on the up in broadcast row? (7)

blocks.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it

annotation.surface: A company doing well despite a public argument.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the up' sounds like a thriving business but literally means airborne; 'row' is a line, not a quarrel.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a company whose business literally goes up into the sky.

entries.clue: Part of Norman arch I cite as following no rules (8)

indicators.note: part of a phrase is a stretch of it, so the answer lies inside the next words

annotation.surface: An architectural guide describing a Norman arch as breaking all the rules.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three clue words; 'as' only joins it to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lawless and chaotic, obeying no rules at all.

entries.clue: Clubs have another go at set of principles (5)

annotation.surface: Golfers retaking a shot to show their principles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Have another go' gives the second piece, so 'at' is left joining it to the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: from the Latin 'I believe', it means a creed, a set of principles.

entries.clue: Country premises finally well-ventilated, written about (5)

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so take the last letter of 'premises'
'about' here means turned about, so the word is written back to front

annotation.surface: An estate agent's description of a country house with airy rooms.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Country premises' reads as a farmhouse, but the definition stops at 'Country'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one country in the Middle East.

entries.clue: Leader at first taking serious action rapidly (4)

indicators.note: at first means at the start, so take each following word's opening letter

annotation.surface: A leader who acts decisively and at speed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'At first' looks like it belongs to 'Leader', but it applies to the four words that follow.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the ruler of imperial Russia, so one kind of leader.

entries.clue: Unrealistic idea? Agree, risible actually at the outset (7)

indicators.note: the outset is the start, so take the opening letter of each word

blocks.note: to chime with something is to agree with it

annotation.surface: Someone conceding that a fanciful notion really is laughable.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark after 'idea' ends the definition, and the next sentence is all wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: named after the mythical monster, it is a fanciful, impossible notion.

entries.clue: Glib talk about a new pet? (7)

indicators.note: about in its sense of 'around': the patter surrounds A and N

blocks.note: a spiel is a slick, well-practised patter

annotation.surface: Someone chattering on about the new pet they've just got.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is by example: this dog is only one kind of pet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a dog breed often kept as a pet, which the question mark admits.

entries.clue: Attempt to include large wager by despicable guy — he’s seen many places (12)

indicators.note: to include something is to take it inside, so GO holds L within it
by means beside, so the next pieces follow on directly

blocks.note: L = large, as on clothing labels
rotter is old British slang for a cad

annotation.surface: A cad placing a big bet on a traveller who has been everywhere.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash splits the clue: everything before it is wordplay, and the definition is a whole phrase after it.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: a traveller who has been all over the world.
